## [FORGEBOT NEPAL-CONTEXT + LICENSE-AWARE SOURCE RETRIEVAL — IMPLEMENTED, TEST FIX IN REVIEW — 2026-10-17]

- **Existing seams extended:** backend/app/services/ai_engine.py::answer_question, backend/app/services/memory_layer.py::retrieve_context_for_prompt, backend/app/services/collectors/openalex.py::_normalize_work, backend/app/services/source_clearance_registry.py, and backend/app/services/research_evidence_assessment.py::openalex_requirement_eligibility. No new source file, provider, model stack, table, or semantic primitive.
- **Nepal-aware answer policy:** ForgeBot considers geographic/jurisdictional/time/practical scope for each question without forcing Nepal into global or other-locality questions; supports Devanagari, Romanized Nepali, English and code-switching; respects dialect/transliteration variation; treats Nepal administrative levels, UTC+05:45, NPR and Bikram Sambat/Gregorian as relevance checks rather than assumptions; avoids demographic inference from name/script/language/location; distinguishes general background from Hami-verified claims; and must not imply browsing/live verification it did not perform. Current/high-consequence facts still require appropriate dated source evidence.
- **Source-rights correction:** OpenAlex's API reference describes OpenAlex dataset data as CC0, but its licensing guide assigns licenses to work locations and its full-text policy says PDFs retain original copyright. Dataset-level CC0 is not used as blanket permission for each abstract. The collector now reconstructs/stores abstract text only when the exact work's primary_location.license is explicitly recognized as CC0, public-domain, or CC BY 4.0. Unknown, non-commercial, no-derivatives, share-alike, and unrecognized licenses stay metadata-only. CC BY abstract excerpts are withheld unless author attribution is available, and the prompt receives authors, title/link, license and license URL. No publisher page or external PDF is fetched.
- **Prompt retrieval:** the existing memory seam links Belief/Pattern records to their source Signals, presents up to three bounded metadata references, excludes malformed/credentialed URLs and non-external/synthetic Signals, and remains read-only. A short OpenAlex abstract excerpt is passed only if the current source clearance, dataset-license tag, per-work license and license URL, attribution rule, exact OpenAlex record identity, collected status, stored content/title match, and retrieval-field declaration all validate. Historical Signals collected before this gate may still contain previously stored abstracts, but the answer retrieval path withholds them unless current per-work license provenance validates; no historic records were deleted.
- **Evidence assessment:** abstract-backed scholarly requirements now also require the per-work reuse license and CC BY attribution. Metadata-only records may support that a literature record exists, but do not satisfy abstract-dependent scholarly observations. Retrieval relevance is not evidence of Nepal/local applicability, current law/policy, or commercial demand.
- **Regression coverage:** test_openalex_abstract_is_not_stored_without_explicit_per_work_license, test_prompt_context_includes_only_provenance_verified_work_licensed_abstract_excerpt, the OpenAlex evidence-eligibility regression, language-aware answer contract, and metadata-only/read-only retrieval tests. These are TEST contracts, not real source collection, model-quality evidence, or a Nepal accuracy benchmark.
- **Truth boundary / remaining limit:** this is source-scoped retrieval, not a comprehensive Nepali knowledge base, trained model, unrestricted web access, or proof that answers are accurate. The Nepal Law Commission remains NOT CLEARED for automated collection in docs/PUBLIC_SOURCES.md because source-use rights were not established. The official AI Policy 2082 listing exists, but its substantive document has not been fully analyzed here. Default MOCK is non-inference output; no real local-model invocation occurred.
- **Latest source/test failure found and corrected in fixture, verification rerun pending:** the 2026-10-16 CI run `38953080112` had 1,325 passed, 2 skipped, and two failures in `tests/test_multi_source_orchestration.py`. Both used manually mocked OpenAlex abstracts with dataset-level CC0 only and omitted work-level license / author provenance. The new work-license gate correctly rejected them. Test fixtures now include an explicit CC BY work-location license, canonical identity, license URL, attribution author and provenance fields. Fixture correction commit: `dc405561ef76c1dfa77d3db98eecb08a0f832aa2`. CI for the previous source SHA `9b6754949723eda3154dfa5a5b1b15cc8cd41336` was still pending/in progress when this change landed; do not infer it passed.
- **Nepali corpus candidate audit:** [Nepali-Flow](https://github.com/Boredoom17/Nepali-Flow) documents 7.1M rows and per-row source/license metadata (IRIISNEPAL, YouTube comments, Wikipedia, and news). Its license guide says news use is source-dependent and recommends filtering commercial use to selected per-row licenses or obtaining news-publisher permissions; its processing guide notes raw, unfiltered comments and no deduplication. This is a language corpus, not a factual knowledge base. Do not bulk ingest, train on, or forward source text without independently verifying row-level rights, source permission, privacy and attribution.
- **Local Nepali model candidate is not approved yet:** [NEPALI-LLM-INSTRUCT-GGUF](https://huggingface.co/mradermacher/NEPALI-LLM-INSTRUCT-GGUF) is a 9B Gemma-2 derivative with quantized files; the Hub page marks the repo Apache-2.0 but identifies Gemma 2 as the base. Google's [Gemma Terms](https://ai.google.dev/gemma/terms/) separately define/use requirements for Gemma and model derivatives. The license metadata needs clarification against upstream terms, and the model card lacks enough evaluated Nepal task metrics to claim production quality. Treat as a local evaluation candidate only after resolving terms and testing Nepali script, Romanized/code-switched language, factual restraint, prompt-injection and citation behavior.
- **Structured knowledge source candidate:** [Wikidata is CC0](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Help:Data_access) and may be useful for multilingual entity/alias and stable-fact grounding, unlike a prose corpus. Its public Query Service requires an identifiable User-Agent, caching and conservative requests and reports limited availability; a source-specific cleared adapter and its exact permitted fields/usage limits are not yet built. Treat it as a research candidate, not a collected source or active capability.
- **Next unblocked action:** confirm the new exact-head CI/security/deployment results. Then examine Wikidata and additional Nepal-authority sources through existing source-clearance policy before deciding whether a genuinely new structured adapter is justified. Nepal-specific current laws, government policies, subnational rules, prices and availability remain UNKNOWN absent properly scoped current primary evidence. Evaluate with an actual authorized local model when available; do not infer inference from test/provider observations.

## [CODE COMPLETE / CI VERIFIED; PRODUCTION KEY REQUIRED] Capability-protected asynchronous public task status (2026-10-11)

- **EXISTING SEAMS INSPECTED:** `backend/app/api/signals.py`, `backend/app/api/analyze.py`, `backend/tests/test_signal_request_demand_api.py`, and `backend/tests/test_step1_router_auth.py`. No new database table or primitive is required.
- **FIRST VERIFIED PRIVACY GAP:** `GET /signals/demand-understanding/{task_id}` returned interpretation state, inferred need ID and unresolved questions from a sequential ID alone. `GET /analyze/{question_id}/status` returned a stored research plan, source results and task progress by sequential ResearchQuestion ID alone. Both endpoints are reachable through the root and `/api` aliases. The legacy analyze UI is currently not part of the active route set; the API still requires a safe contract if enabled.
- **FIX IN SOURCE:** both POST flows now fail before writing when their existing `FORGE_BOT_CONTACT_HMAC_KEY` cannot sign a status capability. Demand polling requires `X-Demand-Understanding-Status-Token`, an HMAC scoped to the WorkerTask ID. Research polling requires `X-Research-Status-Token`, an HMAC bound to both the ResearchQuestion and the submitting Signal. Tokens stay in headers—not paths, query strings or browser history—and invalid/missing tokens get the same 404 as an unknown record. Key rotation invalidates issued capabilities.
- **REGRESSION COVERAGE:** missing/wrong/correct token cases, question-binding replay, idempotent demand submissions returning the same capability, and fail-closed behavior before demand records are written when the signing key is absent.
- **OWNER ACTION STILL REQUIRED:** production needs a strong, unpredictable `FORGE_BOT_CONTACT_HMAC_KEY` (at least 16 characters accepted by the guard; use a long random secret), and the browser/client must retain the returned status-token header securely and send it on polling. These tokens are bearer capabilities; anyone who obtains one can read the scoped status until key rotation.
- **VERIFICATION:** exact-SHA `a6adeef3310efed46ea51250405e844e6ea8c945` is green: **1,058 backend tests passed, 2 skipped**, and frontend tests, typecheck, lint, build, route smoke, evidence-triage tests/typecheck, repository guards, secrets scan, and independent deployment verification all passed. The first `acf4a927` run exposed stale tests after the new capability contract; `a6adeef` corrected those tests without weakening endpoint authorization.
- **NEXT:** keep the production status-token key strong and configured before enabling the gated intake/research flows; validate actual response-header access if any cross-origin browser caller is introduced; continue the remaining GET-data classification sweep. No live production environment values or secrets are accessible through the current Vercel connector.

## [FIXED IN SOURCE — CI PENDING] Protect public booking status with a signed capability (2026-10-11)

- **ROOT CAUSE:** `GET /public/booking-requests/{id}` accepted an enumerable numeric ID as authorization and disclosed a request's service, date/time, and provider response. The existing test only checked that requester name/phone/email/notes were omitted, so it did not catch unauthorized status access.
- **CANONICAL FIX:** booking creation returns a domain-separated HMAC status token. The existing provider flow carries it only in the URL fragment; the browser sends it to the status API as a query parameter, while fragments never leave the browser in the HTTP request. Missing/wrong tokens cannot enumerate a request; wrong tokens return the same 404 as a missing request. Status responses remain PII-minimized, and the status page is `noindex,nofollow`.
- **NO PARALLEL SUBSYSTEM:** the signature uses the existing `FORGE_BOT_CONTACT_HMAC_KEY` already required by the public write-rate limiter, with a separate message namespace. No new table, stored token, or schema migration is added. Public booking creation remains rate-limited and the request remains pending—not accepted or paid.
- **LIMITATION:** rotating `FORGE_BOT_CONTACT_HMAC_KEY` invalidates previously issued status links. If durable links across key rotation become a requirement, add a persisted hashed, per-request capability through the canonical additive migration path.
- **REGRESSION COVERAGE:** the backend test now checks tokenless, wrong-token, valid-token, and no-PII behavior end-to-end; the frontend contract test checks fragment handling and noindex behavior. CI and production runtime behavior must be checked after this commit.

## [DONE WITH LIMITATION] Command 2: open-world discovery engine

- Agent: Grok (executor), owner-authorized direct commits to `origin/main`, 2026-09-30 NPT.
- Scope: build a replaceable discovery capability inside the substrate so Hami can surface things it did not know to look for, without a fixed research workflow or a domain taxonomy. No new table, primitive, service or ledger. See `docs/archive/legacy-docs/FEATURE_INVENTORY.md` § Open-world discovery engine.
- Implementation:
  - `backend/app/services/discovery_engine.py` adds a `DiscoveryMethodRegistry` of versioned plugins and eight built-in methods: `evidence_contradiction`, `question_reframe`, `numeric_divergence`, `disconnection`, `isolation`, `recurrence`, `capability_integrity` and `refuted_basis_stop`.
  - Findings persist only as ENTITY + EVIDENCE + RELATION + EVENT. Entities are validated by `type_registry.schema_json`. Evidence stays `possible`/`hypothesized` with basis provenance. Relations are `derived_from` (hypothesized), or `may_relate`/`reframes`/`stops` (possible). Events are `discovery_run_completed` and `discovery_deferred`.
  - An unknown finding kind is registered as a proposed `entity_type` and deferred until activated through `set_type_status`.
  - Unmet method inputs become a proposed `discovery_input` CAPABILITY plus a `capability_gap` finding. Only a capability that `provides` the input and has a verified activation record satisfies it.
  - The discovery vocabulary is registered through `register_type` → `set_type_status` on the first persisted run, not in `seed_core_types`, so a deploy writes nothing.
  - Endpoints: `GET /forge/substrate/discovery/{methods,preview,findings}` and `POST /forge/substrate/discovery/runs`, private under `FORGE_API_KEY`. The engine is not wired into the scheduled cycle and makes no network calls.
- Proof (`backend/tests/test_discovery_engine.py`, 11 tests):
  - In a world recorded through the canonical services, one run surfaces three things. First, a contradiction on a need that has supported and refuted evidence, citing both evidence ids. Second, a reframed question whose premise that need is. Third, a capability gap for a pre-contract `active` capability with no attributable pass.
  - Every engine output is `possible`/`hypothesized` and cites resolvable rows. The inspected relation's truth is unchanged.
  - An empty substrate yields nothing. Reruns add only the run event.
  - A missing input creates a proposed gap row. An unverified "active" provider does not close it. Building, testing and activating the gap row does close it.
  - A new kind is proposed and deferred, and materializes after activation, with no new table.
  - Fabricated, basis-less and overclaiming findings are rejected, and a crashing plugin is isolated.
  - A measured 2.8x price difference yields an observation and a research question. A shared address across an organization and a need yields a `possible` `may_relate` hypothesis. That relation cannot reach `tested` without evidence. After it is refuted by recorded evidence, the next run emits `reason_to_stop`.
  - An unanswered question with two empty research tasks is reframed. Isolation and recurrence are detected.
  - Methods are replaceable. Preview writes nothing, and the endpoints return 401 without the key when one is set.
  - Mutation checks: disabling finding validation, or counting the engine's own relations as connections, makes the corresponding tests fail.
- Verification (local): backend `pytest` 575 passed, 2 skipped (only the opt-in live GDELT/OpenAlex checks). `git diff --check` is clean. The root app was not touched.
- GitHub Actions (OBSERVED): run `36743983066` on `1b1b63a`. The `backend` job (the required check) succeeded. The `frontend` job failed only at `npm test`, as on every commit since `2b11fb5`, because the root app has no tests. The workflow change needs the `workflow` token scope. The push was accepted with the remote notice `Required status check "backend" is expected.` (admin enforcement is off).
- Current limitation: the engine only proposes. No discovery has been run against production data (by instruction), so nothing about the real production substrate has been discovered yet. The built-in methods cover the recorded substrate only. External comparisons (prices, time series, other markets) need cleared sources declared as input tags and are surfaced as capability gaps until then. Discovery questions are not yet handed to `ResearchQuestion` or the planner automatically.
- Owner action still required: decide whether and when to run `POST /forge/substrate/discovery/runs` against production. This writes discovery rows and registers the discovery vocabulary. Production answered `401` to an unauthenticated `GET /api/forge/substrate/types` on 2026-09-30 (OBSERVED), so `FORGE_API_KEY` is set there and these endpoints are key-gated.
- Next removable dependency: an explicit, reviewed hand-off from discovery `question` entities to `ResearchQuestion` rows, so cleared collectors can gather evidence that advances or refutes them.

## [FUTURE CAPABILITY — NOT IMPLEMENTED] Authorized prospect discovery and response path

### Owner-dependency ranking — production snapshot 2026-09-29

**Rank 1: acquiring a legitimate real need/opportunity without the owner
supplying it.** This is the first blocked seam on the production path to money:
production currently exposes 0 opportunities, 0 products, and a revenue
breakdown of 0 potential, 0 expected, and 0 realized revenue. `/api/health`
reports PostgreSQL available and ready, and `/api/forge/runtime` reports a
completed cycle, 10 signals, and 4 outcome rows; cycle execution and row
counts are not commercial validation. The public Feed contains 11 items; its
inspected belief is explicitly uncorroborated, and the inspected pattern is
derived from Crossref scholarly metadata. Neither is buyer demand.

The code confirms why this dependency remains:

- `source_clearance_registry` contains five exact-purpose entries, none
  supporting `authorized_prospect_discovery`; the readiness test asserts that
  this yields no eligible source, no external request, and no candidate.
- `collector_runner` explicitly excludes GitHub, Reddit, RSS, news, and arXiv
  from standing collection until cleared. The separate GitHub bounty module
  has a public-search helper, but no runtime caller for its fetch/ingest
  functions; its claim mutation requires `GITHUB_TOKEN`. Existing bounty tests
  also accept a public issue with no amount as an Opportunity with unknown
  price and low confidence, so that adapter cannot by itself establish a
  funded offer or verified revenue.
- `/api/signals/public-request` can receive a request from an external person,
  and the demand worker can classify it as `possible_demand`; neither discovers
  or attracts that person. Research collection and the public Feed do not
  establish customer pain, buyer interest, or willingness to pay.

**Exact owner dependency:** provide a genuine inbound need through the existing
intake, or obtain/review source-specific authority for a bounded source that
can reveal real commercial demand. Forge cannot remove this dependency merely
by querying a publicly reachable endpoint. Existing automated work includes
the intelligence cycle, bounded demand understanding after submission, source
clearance checks, capability search, and evidence-gated economic assessment.

**Why no economic implementation is made in this task:** the source registry
has no applicable authorization, and no genuine opportunity exists to advance.
Adding a collector or enabling the uncleared GitHub helper would bypass the
existing source-authorization boundary; fabricating a demand record would not
reduce owner actions on a real transaction. The external unblock is a current,
documented source authorization and bounded permitted operation/fields. Once
that exists, a source-specific adapter can be assessed against existing
Signal/Evidence/Opportunity machinery.

### Repaired in this pass

1. **`backend/scripts/recovery_verify.py` was broken — the recovery drill could not verify anything.** It asserted a frozen `signals == 11847` against a database holding 11,860 rows, so it exited 1 on every run and any real recovery would have looked like a failure. It now proves the real invariants instead of a remembered number: the snapshot must restore with `integrity_check=ok`, no foreign-key violations, no leftover `*_old`/`*_new` rebuild tables, and per-table row counts **equal to the live file**; a mismatch names the failing table. Added `backend/tests/test_recovery_verify.py` (5 tests) covering the faithful snapshot, growth with real data, a deliberately lossy snapshot (detected), a missing database, and the backup-directory guarantee below.
2. **A live data-loss hazard in the same drill.** A drill that reused the canonical `storage/backups` directory with `safe_backup(..., keep=1)` would have pruned the operator's real recovery points down to the newest one. The drill now always writes its snapshot to a private temporary directory and restores `backup.BACKUPS_DIR` afterwards; the new test asserts an existing operator snapshot survives untouched.
3. **Two authority documents asserted a false current fact.** `docs/PUBLICITY_GATE.md` and `docs/CURRENT_FOCUS.md` both stated that production `/api/health` and the public API returned HTTP 500. Production is healthy (table above), so the gate's boxes were re-evaluated from dated command output: `/api/health` and `/api/public/providers` are now checked; the two owner-controlled boxes (footer domain, contact mailbox) stay open; provider availability stays open but is now recorded as **empty, not unknown**. The mailbox note was itself stale — `SITE.email` is empty, so no `mailto:` is published anywhere and the earlier `hello@pending-domain.local` no longer exists in the rendered HTML or `src/lib/content.ts`. Also removed an orphan fragment line above the `docs/CURRENT_FOCUS.md` heading.
4. **The deployed API had no reachable machine-readable contract.** `app.main._alias_app_routes_under_api` skipped `/openapi.json` when mirroring root routes under `/api`, and only `/api/*` reaches the Python service on Vercel, so nothing could read the schema in production: `/openapi.json` answered the frontend SPA HTML and `/api/openapi.json` answered 404, even though the document itself generates correctly (282,611 bytes, `openapi 3.1.0`). The mirror now covers the schema (`include_in_schema=False`, so the published document is unchanged), and the interactive `/docs` and `/redoc` pages stay deliberately unaliased because their HTML points at `/openapi.json`, which the frontend rewrite would answer with the SPA — aliasing them would have shipped a broken page. Verified on the reloaded local service: `/api/openapi.json` returns 200 `application/json`, byte-identical to `/openapi.json`; `/api/docs` correctly stays 404. Added `backend/tests/test_api_ingress_alias.py` (4 tests: mirrored health, schema reachable, alias equal to root document, `/api/*` absent from the published schema). ## [DONE] Scheduled discovery integration (2026-10-09, corrected 2026-10-09)

- **Implementation:** `GET /scheduled/intelligence` now runs a 5th stage using
  `app.services.discovery_engine.run_discovery` with `max_findings_per_method=10`.
  The stage uses a separate DB session, commits only on success, rolls back on
  failure, and returns only an operational summary (counts of methods_run,
  methods_total, surfaced, existing, rejected, deferred, errors, capability_gaps).
  Per-method failure isolation is preserved; a discovery failure does not prevent
  other stages.
- **Work bound (corrected):** Uses `itertools.islice` for genuine early-stop —
  the lazy iterator is consumed only up to the limit, not materialized first.
  **Limitation:** This bounds findings *consumed*, not DB rows scanned or time
  spent. Methods that eagerly build large lists before their first yield are not
  bounded by this. Per-method work characteristics are documented in method
  docstrings.
- **Methods count (corrected):** `methods_run` counts only methods with
  `status=="ran"`, not those blocked by missing capabilities or errored before
  execution. `methods_total` reports the registry size for context.
- **Qualification gates preserved:** The `curiosity_questions` method calls
  `CuriosityEngine.find_unexplored_patterns()` which enforces the bibliographic
  background filter and commercial qualification gate. Findings are emitted with
  `epistemic_state="hypothesized"` and `facets.confirmed=False` — never as validated.
- **Authorization:** Existing `CRON_SECRET` Bearer auth unchanged. No new entity
  types activated automatically. No findings converted to commercial bets.
  No actions executed. No human contact, spending, or public publication.
- **Routine owner action removed:** Manual triggering of discovery runs; the

## 2026-10-14 — prevent fixed-window discovery starvation (verified at main snapshot 4f44cffe)

- Existing seam inspected: backend/app/services/discovery_engine.py::run_discovery, WorldEvent, and the existing discovery_run_completed EVENT. The engine previously consumed the same first max_findings_per_method outputs on every run; idempotency made those rows existing, but they still exhausted the window, so later stable findings could be starved indefinitely.
- Change: persist versioned, opaque per-method cursor digests inside the existing discovery_run_completed EVENT. Persisted runs resume after the last consumed finding and wrap when they reach the end; a missing cursor resets the method safely. Preview remains read-only. Cursor state never stores the raw finding key and creates no table, new primitive, side ledger, or external permission.
- Test: added a deterministic five-candidate / two-per-run regression. It verifies three runs surface candidates 1–5 in order, cursor values are digests rather than raw keys, and wraparound is idempotent.
- Owner action removed: no new routine action is needed to advance a method beyond its initial output window. The change does not contact people, spend money, activate a provider, or declare outcomes.
- Remaining: finding generators can still be expensive to scan, and methods with nondeterministic ordering can cause cursor resets. Production scheduling/run persistence must be independently observed; source and tests alone do not prove natural cron execution.
- Verification: exact-head CI passed with the cursor regression included (1,303 backend passed, 2 skipped); all nine jobs succeeded, independent deployment verification passed for the same SHA, and secrets scan passed. Natural scheduled execution remains unverified.

## 2026-11-03 — D97 post-festival wholesale stock returnability (UNKNOWN; manual-only)

### Source-backed legal and tax baseline

- **Muluki Civil Code 2074, Chapter 6 (sale contracts), Nepal Law Commission:** section 545 defines a sale contract and permits conditional or unconditional terms. Sections 551–552 address satisfactory quality and rejection/replacement of goods that do not conform to the contract. Section 554 makes ownership transfer depend on contract terms, party conduct and circumstances. Section 555 assigns risk of physical loss/damage to the seller until delivery unless the contract says otherwise; it does not expressly allocate market-demand or obsolescence risk. Sections 556–557 address inspection and deemed acceptance, including receipt, storing after inspection, and failure to promptly reject. Section 561 allows the seller to claim damages when a buyer refuses to accept after a sale contract. This is a delivery/acceptance/conformity framework, not proof of a post-festival buyback right.
- **Consumer Protection Act 2075:** section 2(d) defines a consumer by consumption/use; section 14's seven-day return route is a consumer-facing right subject to its conditions. It is not evidence that a retailer can return stock bought for resale to a distributor after a season.
- **IRD FAQ:** where a registered person claimed input VAT but could not sell goods because their expiry period passed, IRD says a debit note may be issued and the goods returned. The FAQ also describes debit/credit notes for post-sale price adjustment or returned goods and lists invoice, supplier/recipient, item, reason, amount and tax details. This is tax-accounting treatment for a return that is permitted; it does not itself create the contractual right to return seasonal carryover.
- IRD's current VAT-rules index lists the 27th amendment (18 Poush 2082); the linked rules body was not inspected in this pass. The FAQ page is not separately date-stamped.

### Finding and correction

- **D97 remains UNKNOWN.** No public Nepali supplier/distributor policy or directly observed post-festival return negotiation was found in this bounded search. Fashion carryover, electronics, seasonal decor, FMCG expiry, consignment and stock-on-approval may have materially different terms; do not generalize from one category.
- Correct the earlier shorthand in the D97 question: the inspected Civil Code text does not establish that title *and* obsolescence risk automatically pass on delivery. Ownership and acceptance depend on the contract and conduct; section 555 is specifically risk of loss/damage. No conclusion about actual local practice follows from the statute alone.
- The seven-day consumer return provision and the expiry-stock debit-note answer must not be conflated with a B2B right to return conforming, unsold seasonal stock.

### Existing Hami seam and candidate capability

- Reuse the existing ENTITY / RELATION / EVENT / EVIDENCE / CAPABILITY / ACTION primitives: supplier, retailer, SKU/lot, shipment and invoice; supplies/consignment/return-window/credit terms; delivery, inspection, acceptance, return request, rejection, credit note, transfer, markdown and write-off events; consented contract/invoice/credit-note evidence with source, date, scope and condition.
- Candidate reusable capability: **stock-returnability and recovery assessment**. It would extract the written return/consignment/credit terms, distinguish defect/expiry from seasonal demand, compare eligible routes (return, credit, transfer/resale, markdown, donation or lawful recycling), and produce an evidence-backed disposition packet. This is a proposal, NOT IMPLEMENTED; no new model/table/primitive is justified.
- It could remove manual comparison of purchase terms, delivery/acceptance dates, return windows and credit-note conditions. That owner-dependent step is not removed yet because no public contract or consented merchant document has been examined.

### Priority, blockers and next dependency

- Consequence/reuse are potentially meaningful because inventory loss, supplier credit and future stocking interact; local incidence, recoverable value, frequency and willingness to use a service remain unmeasured. Feasibility is moderate only after real documents and category scope exist. Privacy/legal risk is manageable only with consent, redaction and clear document-use rights.
- Next dependency: a public supplier return policy or owner-authorized, consented and redacted purchase/consignment terms, invoice and credit-note examples from independent retailer–supplier pairs, with product category and delivery/acceptance dates. No contact or private-record request is authorized in this run.
- Manual research only: Law Commission/IRD robots, terms and reuse scope were not reviewed; no runtime source registration, collection, persistence or provider transmission occurred.



## 2026-11-04 — D96 subcase: GB electricity connections data and Gate 1→Gate 2 readiness (UNKNOWN; manual-only)

### What the sources establish

- **Ofgem, *Transforming Connections Data*, published 25 September 2026; response deadline 6 November 2026.** The 91-page consultation reports stakeholder concerns about difficulty obtaining a complete, consistent picture of connection queues, reinforcement activity and future network needs. It proposes a new Demand Capacity Register (DCR), a Distribution Works Report (DWR), and changes to the TEC, ECR, TWR and TORI datasets. This is a first-phase policy consultation; responses inform later policy and possible statutory consultations. It is not proof that the proposed registers or standards are already operational.
- **DCR proposal:** persistent unique project, connection and applicant identifiers; quote issue date; record creation and last-updated dates; application status; location/capacity; and references to reinforcement work. **DWR proposal:** a persistent reinforcement-package identifier, a package table and asset-change table, links to dependent connection projects/network needs, and at least quarterly publication with event-driven updates for new or materially changed reinforcement projects. Detailed reporting requirements remain subject to consultation and subsequent statutory consultation.
- **Data quality:** Ofgem describes validity, consistency, uniqueness, integrity and reasonableness as distinct dimensions. It explicitly says a complete data-quality framework will not be introduced through this consultation because common standards and fair measures need further work. This is a documented unfinished standardisation layer, not proof that any particular publisher or project has failed.
- **NESO TEC Register page, read 4 November:** the page labels the dataset as updated twice weekly and shows a CSV named `tec-register-03-november-2026.csv`, with a “last changed” time about four hours before retrieval. It warns that capacity aggregated across stages and technology types can produce duplicate entries, and that corrections may take longer under a temporary data-change governance process. The CSV itself was not retrieved: its download redirected to a signed object-storage URL inaccessible to the browser. - **NGED, October 2026 Gate 1→Gate 2 notice and page, read 4 November:** the notice says the next NESO application window has not yet been announced. The regional page offers Option A (reassess the distribution offer now) and Option B (use the indicative offer through a future NESO window); Option B is currently closed. NGED says a reassessed point of connection, works, costs and timescales may change again after the NESO process or transmission-impact assessment. This applies to NGED customers in South Wales, South West and the Midlands, not all GB projects.
- **Version guard:** NESO's Gate 2 Criteria Methodology dated 21 January 2026 explicitly labels itself not a live methodology. The evidence-handbook page says the previous evidence window is closed and the guidance remains for re-submissions after initial checks. Do not use these documents as a current checklist for new submissions.

## 2026-11-05 — D95 cold-storage operationalization and market reconciliation (candidate; manual-only)

### Evidence and scope

- PMAMP's *Status & Effectiveness of Cold Rooms/Cold Chambers Established Under PMAMP* (FY 2081/82; published year 2082/2025) describes 87 PMAMP units through FY 2080/81 in its executive summary, but the figure caption and §1.3 say FY 2072/73–2079/80; the province table totals 87 while the methodology refers to an 86-unit secondary inventory. It sampled 25/87 purposively through field visits, questionnaires and FGDs in five districts. The sample has zero sites from Madhes (9 listed) and Karnali (1 listed). Survey dates are not specified; the report notes non-digitized records, self-report bias and incomplete seasonal observation. A separate 126-store inventory appears in the literature review and is not reconciled to the PMAMP 87/86 series.
- The same study reports seven sites at full capacity and one nonfunctional for lack of an adopted business model. Its Mustang Dhamang Krishak Samuha 20-ton apple store reported Rs 50,000 monthly revenue, Rs 20,000 monthly profit and 1–2% spoilage; a Rupandehi 10MT fish store reported 0.1% utilization and no current revenue. Commodity, geography and operating model differ; neither case represents the national inventory.
- PMAMP's FY 2082/83 manual (publication year 2083 Asar; exact Gregorian day not stated) says only some cold stores operate at full capacity and most are partial or closed, without an asset denominator/cutoff. It says crop-specific SOPs are absent, while providing temperature/humidity/storage-duration reference values and general daily/weekly/monthly maintenance guidance. Its 200MT economics are explicitly illustrative: assumed 80–90% utilization yields Rs 9 lakh revenue versus Rs 11 lakh costs (Rs 6.4 lakh electricity); a 50% electricity subsidy changes the modeled Rs 2 lakh loss to Rs 1.2 lakh profit. This is not measured facility performance.
- Kathmandu Post, 11 June 2026, reports a separate Sudurpashchim provincial programme: 13 facilities, six structures complete, seven stalled, only one of six operational at reporting time, >Rs 52.5m spent against Rs 81.5m initial estimate, and one farmer transporting 5.5 tonnes of potato seed about 124km to Pahalmanpur. The article reports operating-procedure, handover, electricity and technician issues. It is one secondary source; no primary provincial progress record was retrieved. Do not combine its 13 with PMAMP's 87/86.
- Department of Agriculture's AMPIS app notice was published 28 July 2026 for 12 federal agricultural markets. AMPIS showed data dated 2083 Kartik 18 / 4 November 2026. Its undated technical note says 11 markets use a min/max midpoint and Kalimati uses an arithmetic mean from multiple observations since 2083 Asar 1; the note says these indicators are not directly comparable. Wholesale prices alone do not establish farmgate netback or include matched grade, logistics, storage, commission, handling, spoilage or buyer terms.

### Consequence and capability

- The real consequence is not simply “too few cold rooms”: an existing asset can be physically complete but lack power, technicians, maintenance, crop handling, a viable operating model or nearby market volume. A high-occupancy facility may still have weak net economics; a low-occupancy facility may be unsuitable for its catchment/commodity. Farmers may still sell quickly, travel farther or absorb spoilage, but no national loss total or current facility-level status is established.
- Candidate reusable capability: **asset-to-operation-to-market reconciliation**. Reuse ENTITY / RELATION / EVENT / EVIDENCE / CAPABILITY / ACTION to link facility, owner/operator, commodity, season, capacity, dated operating state, temperature/humidity, power, maintenance, intake/outflow, spoilage, costs/revenue, market price method, transport and buyer outcome. Require source-specific cutoff and method; do not rank facilities by capacity or occupancy alone. This extends D95, not a new unknown or taxonomy. NOT IMPLEMENTED; no new model/table/collector.

- At main `1f4d2626`, `SourceCollector.normalize` uses `raw_item.get("provenance") or metadata`, so a nonempty explicit provenance object can omit fields held only in nested metadata. The runner passes normalized metadata to ObserverEngine and merges selected task/authorization context; ObserverEngine persists top-level provenance and publication/retrieval times on Signal; `_ensure_evidence` copies Signal provenance/timestamps to Evidence. `assess_source_record` computes publication age from published_at versus retrieved_at only; `_evidence_citation` exposes registry ID and retrieval time but not source-effective cutoff, method or version. Contract risk only; no production data loss demonstrated.
- No PMAMP, AMPIS or DoA source entry exists in `source_clearance_registry.py`. Exact robots/terms/reuse review was incomplete or yielded no reuse grant. Keep these sources MANUAL-ONLY / NOT CLEARED for automated collection, persistence or provider transmission. No source registration, collector run, Signal/Evidence write or provider transmission occurred.

Do not contact operators/farmers, request private records or publish a recommendation without explicit authorization. **Practical implication.** The recoverable value is not “cold-room capacity” alone. It is the lifecycle gap between grant/contract, construction, commissioning tests, handover, operator, continuous operation, usable capacity, crop/season, power/maintenance, throughput, quality loss, logistics and market. “Built”, “completed”, “commissioned”, “operating”, “continuously operating”, “capacity used” and “throughput” are separate states.

**Existing Hami mapping; no new schema.**
- ENTITY: programme (PMAMP/NAMP as one renamed entity), provincial grant programme, facility, PIU, local government, operator, crop, market, power/transport infrastructure.
- RELATION: funded_by, located_in, owned_by, operated_by, handed_over_to, serves_crop, connected_to_collection/transport/market.
- EVENT: grant, contract, construction, upgrade, completion, commissioning test, handover, operation, outage, maintenance, storage cycle, sale.
- EVIDENCE: source identity, report version, publication/listing/body date, audit period, source-declared cutoff, geography, count denominator, capacity definition, method, and the exact supported claim.
- CAPABILITY: cooling, ripening, power reliability, technician, maintenance, grading, storage scheduling and logistics.
- ACTION: only later, authorized repair/commissioning/handover/booking/route coordination; none was performed here.

## 2026-11-08 — D98 disaster credit, insurance recovery and customs-service continuity (manual-only; D98 remains UNKNOWN)

### Source-backed observations

- **Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), Circular No. 5 (A/B/C), FY 2083/84 — primary source.** The official circular archive lists it on 13 October 2026. The one-page PDF was inspected visually. It adds clause 46 to Unified Directive 2/2082 for Class A, B and C licensed banks/financial institutions. After a realistic analysis of sales/income, cash flow, cash reserves, import/export effects and loan utilization, an institution *may* extend the payment period for an instalment (principal and/or interest) due at the end of Asoj 2083 until the end of Poush 2083 for: enterprises/projects/businesses directly affected in Bhotekoshi or Budhi Gandaki flood-affected areas; businesses based on importing/exporting raw, semi-finished or finished goods through Rasuwa customs; and affected borrowers in flood-affected areas. This is discretionary permission, not an automatic moratorium, blanket deferral, proof of lender uptake, or proof that any named borrower qualifies. It does not establish the treatment of every loan product or Class D institution.
  - Archive: https://www.nrb.org.np/category/circulars/
  - Circular PDF/page: https://www.nrb.org.np/bfr/%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%B0%E0%A4%BF%E0%A4%AA%E0%A4%A4%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B0-%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%82-%E0%A5%AB-%E0%A4%95-%E0%A4%96-%E0%A4%97-%E0%A5%A8%E0%A5%A6%E0%A5%AE%E0%A5%A9-%E0%A5%AE%E0%A5%AA-%E0%A4%A8/
- **NRB, Notice No. 12/2083-84 — primary source, adjacent trade-continuity signal.** The official archive lists it on 6 November 2026; its one-page PDF was inspected. It asks Class A/B/C banks and financial institutions to keep necessary banking services available from branches located at customs offices during public holidays from 2083/07/22 through 2083/07/26, to support customs clearance, trade facilitation, supply continuity and service flow during Tihar. It is not a disaster-relief rule, does not identify Rasuwa as the only covered customs office, and does not prove a specific branch operated or an importer benefited.
  - Notice PDF/page: https://www.nrb.org.np/bfr/%E0%A4%B8%E0%A5%82%E0%A4%9A%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%BE-%E0%A4%A8%E0%A4%82-%E0%A5%A7%E0%A5%A8-%E0%A5%A6%E0%A5%AE%E0%A5%A9-%E0%A5%AE%E0%A5%AA-%E0%A4%AD%E0%A4%A8%E0%A5%8D%E0%A4%B8%E0%A4%BE%E0%A4%B0/
- **NRB, Current Macroeconomic and Financial Situation, first two months of 2026/27 — primary context, not flood evidence.** The report published 15 October uses a two-month national reporting period ending around mid-September. It reports BFI credit of Rs 5,950.58 billion, 15.6% of outstanding credit backed by current assets, wholesale/retail credit growth of 2.5%, trust-receipt import credit growth of 9.4%, working-capital demand-loan growth of 1.4%, cash-credit contraction of 1.3%, overdraft contraction of 1.2%, and an NPL ratio of 5.66% at mid-July. These are national aggregates with different cutoffs; they do not measure flood-affected borrowers, post-flood arrears, or actual use of Circular No. 5.
  - https://www.nrb.org.np/red/current-macroeconomic-and-financial-situation-english-based-on-two-months-data-of-2026-27/
- **Nepal Insurance Authority (NIA) — official index evidence, document bodies not retrieved.** The official NIA homepage lists both “Rasuwa Flood Claim Settlement Abbreviated Procedure, 2083” and “Insurance claim details of damage caused by floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers.” Its circular index separately lists “Insurance payment simplification” dated 2 October 2026. The procedure PDF and claim-detail data body were not retrieved from the official site; the index proves the listed resources exist, not their contents or current claim outcomes.
  - Homepage: https://www.nia.gov.np/
  - Circular index: https://nia.gov.np/law/circular
- **Secondary reporting on the NIA Rasuwa procedure.** The Rising Nepal (1 October 2026) reports that, for the 26 August Bhotekoshi/Trishuli disaster, insurers may settle technically uncomplicated claims up to Rs 500,000 without appointing an external surveyor, may make advances up to 50% of estimated claims, and cannot reject solely because the usual filing deadline elapsed. It reports that where physical inspection/documents are unavailable, photos/videos, digital records, government records, financial statements and tax records may be used. It also reports 18 insurers had received 2,180 claims estimated at Rs 20.99 billion by 28 September, while Rs 6.748 million had been paid including advances. These are secondary, time-bounded reported figures: claims received/estimated versus payments at that snapshot, not final liabilities, adjudicated claims, denial rates, or proof of delay.

This is not a substitute for the unread official procedure.
  - https://notebazar.com/news/2026/09/29/169214/
- **Separate life/micro-life lead.** Nepal News (3 November 2026) reports an eight-point NIA circular for life and micro-life policyholders affected by the 26 August flood, including a six-month extension for premiums and policy-loan instalments without interest or penalties and simplified death-claim procedures. The official PDF was not retrieved. NIA's official index lists a payment-simplification item dated 2 October, but it has not been established that this is the same instrument. Keep this secondary report separate from non-life property/stock claims and from NRB bank-loan relief.

### Scope and truth boundaries

- The 26 August 2026 Bhotekoshi–Trishuli–Narayani disaster and the October 2026 Gorkha–Budhi Gandaki disaster remain separate events. NRB Circular No. 5 expressly spans Bhotekoshi and Budhi Gandaki affected areas and Rasuwa-customs-linked import/export businesses. The NIA Rasuwa procedure and the 3 November life/micro-life report concern the August 26 event. Do not transfer NIA Rasuwa procedure terms to the October Gorkha event.
- D98's Chaurasiya Rs 4.5 crore uninsured-stock account remains an anecdotal lead. No verified location, lender, loan class, policy, customs dependency or eligibility link ties that case to Circular No. 5. No borrower-specific deferral, missed instalment, insurance payment or final settlement is established.
- The Rs 20.99 billion and Rs 6.748 million figures are a secondary 28 September snapshot of estimated claims received and payments including advances. Their difference is a reason to seek later claim-status evidence, not proof of denial, insurer failure or a final unpaid liability.
- The 6 November customs-branch notice is a separate trade-continuity action, not evidence of disaster recovery or a specific Rasuwa customs reopening.

### Practical value and six-primitive mapping

- The concrete value is preserving recoverable business assets and liquidity after a shock, while keeping trade channels operating. The same affected business may need two distinct evidence views: an insurer claim view (policy/covered interest, asset or stock identity, pre-loss condition, damage, inventory/invoice/tax evidence, claim estimate and status) and a lender instalment-relief view (lender/class/product, due date, sales/income, cash flow, cash reserves, import/export impact, loan utilization and lender decision). Evidence may overlap, but insurer and lender requirements are not interchangeable.
- Reuse the existing primitives: ENTITY (business, asset/stock, insurer, bank, customs office, location); RELATION (insured-by, borrowed-from, located-in, supplied-by, import/export-through); EVENT (flood, stock loss, claim filed, instalment due, extension requested/decided, advance/final payment, customs service window); EVIDENCE (policy/circular, source date and cutoff, invoice, inventory/tax/financial record, photo/video, government record, claim or lender decision); CAPABILITY (source-time-aware recovery-rule reconciliation and consented evidence-packet completeness); ACTION (request, submission, decision, payment) only when separately authorized.
- A reusable Hami capability could assemble a user-controlled, provenance-preserving recovery evidence packet and render separate insurer/lender requirement views. This protects value even where the final result is not revenue; it can generalize to other disasters and jurisdictions without making Hami an insurer, lender, legal adviser or emergency authority.

### Existing Hami seam, owner dependency and exact blocker

- Existing path only: SourceCollector.normalize → collector_runner → ObserverEngine → Signal → Evidence → research_evidence_assessment → research_synthesis_engine._evidence_citation. Signal/Evidence already store published_at, retrieved_at and provenance. SourceCollector.normalize returns raw_item.provenance **or** metadata; if explicit provenance is nonempty, metadata-only source-effective cutoff/version/method/scope fields may be omitted. collector_runner adds selected task and registry fields, not arbitrary metadata. ObserverEngine serializes metadata["provenance"] to Signal; Evidence copies it. Assessment freshness is publication date versus retrieval time. Citation exposes registry ID and retrieval time, but not source-effective cutoff, version or method. This is a contract risk; no production data loss is demonstrated.
- WebCollector uses an HTMLParser for visible HTML text, truncates to 1,500 characters, and does not parse the NRB/NIA PDF bodies. No existing PDF parser was found in the targeted source search. Do not add a collector or parser now: source rights are not cleared and source-code editing remains blocked.
- **Owner-dependent step removed this run:** none in the external workflow. The public-source discovery and rule cross-reference were completed internally without owner contact. A future capability could remove repeated manual cross-document chronology and evidence-requirement reconciliation. It cannot remove source-rights review, the affected person's consent, insurer/surveyor review, or a lender's independent decision.
- **Exact blockers:** NRB has no identified explicit reuse grant and its robots endpoint was inaccessible; NIA copyright policy requires prior written permission for commercial reuse (subject to the policy's stated fair-dealing exception) and its robots endpoint was inaccessible; official NIA PDF/data bodies remain unread; no NRB/NIA source is registered; WebCollector is HTML-only; source-write safety remains blocked; operational open ResearchQuestion records remain behind the owner-key read boundary.

Feasibility: high for manual public-source reconciliation, low for automated ingestion/action until rights and source editing are resolved. ### Existing seam and priority
- Reuse existing ENTITY/RELATION/EVENT/EVIDENCE/CAPABILITY/ACTION and Signal/Evidence provenance. Current source path: `backend/app/services/collectors/base.py::SourceCollector.normalize` → `backend/app/services/collector_runner.py::execute_task` → `backend/app/services/observer_engine.py::ObserverEngine.observe/_ensure_evidence` → `backend/app/services/research_evidence_assessment.py::assess_source_record` → `backend/app/services/research_synthesis_engine.py::_evidence_citation`.
- `Signal` and `Evidence` already store `published_at`, `retrieved_at` and JSON provenance. `normalize` uses `raw_item.provenance or metadata`, which can drop metadata-only source-time fields when explicit provenance is non-empty. ### Real-world consequence and reusable capability

The public record exposes two sides of a humanitarian supply chain: district-level dispatch totals and later organization-level distribution totals. There is no shared shipment identifier or public record joining dispatched lot → transfer/receipt → distribution point → household/beneficiary reach → outcome. The quantities are not directly additive: actors, geography, dates, units and item categories differ. This is an observability/reconciliation gap, not evidence that goods were lost, withheld or under-delivered.

Reuse the existing six primitives and existing substrate:
- ENTITY: NDRRMA, DAO/EOCs, NRCS, district chapters, municipalities, assets, distribution points and recipient groups where legitimately identified.
- RELATION: responsible-for, dispatched-to, received-by, coordinated-with and served-by.
- EVENT: report snapshot, dispatch, transfer, receipt, distribution, evacuation and restoration.
- EVIDENCE: source URL, exact report/page/version, source-declared cutoff, publication/listing date, retrieval time, geography, unit, denominator and epistemic class.
- CAPABILITY: reconcile state transitions and coexisting observations without collapsing unlike measures.
- ACTION: no contact, allocation or operational action absent explicit authorization.

## 2026-11-19 — M7-H NACK-responder bypass (011 follow-on; diagnostic, inconclusive)

- **Existing seam/history:** traced the existing client API and harness publisher-PC creation in `services/hami-media/main.go` (`git log --follow`, `git log -S`, and `git blame`; original API seam in `4f22ec18d`). The M7-H harness publishers are created separately from the SFU's router peers and viewer clients, so the bypass is confined to the harness publisher API.
- **Change:** M7-H harness publisher peers use a separate Pion API that retains default codecs, NACK generation, RTCP reports, simulcast headers, stats, and TWCC, but omits only `nack.ResponderInterceptor` (`main.go:5374-5409`, `5494-5502`, `5653-5655`). Viewer APIs and SFU-side peers retain their defaults. No protected constant changed.
- **Build:** Go `go1.27.4 darwin/arm64`; `go build -ldflags="-X main.routerUDPMuxMode=disabled -X main.routerSocketWriteMode=enabled -X main.clientSocketReadMode=enabled -X main.clientSocketReadBufferSize=4194304" -o /tmp/hami-media-011-nack-bypass .` succeeded. `go version -m` confirms the exact ldflags in `/tmp/hami-media-011-nack-bypass`.
- **Run evidence:** `/tmp/hami-media-011-nack-bypass-run-log`, with `ulimit -n 65536`. The SFU logged 35 one-second samples with `packets=0 staleOver500ms=3000` (lines 24031–48094); later packets resumed, but line 95229 still reports 2,915 stale publishers. The harness did not emit `frames=0 staleOver500ms=3000` (zero matching samples); at line 96007 it was still sending 14,276 frames with one stale publisher.
- **Outcome:** the proof exited 1 at the viewer readiness check: `hami-sfu-viewer-86` received 2 packets where 5 were required (lines 139131–139134). Aggregate viewer passes and p95/p99 are **NOT MEASURABLE**.
- **Profiles and verdict:** no profile files were produced because the existing profile hook requires all 3,000 harness publishers to have `frames=0` and be stale (`main.go:3569-3572`), which did not happen. Consequently fdMutex/NACK profile counts are unavailable. **INCONCLUSIVE** for the exact harness stall signature; the SFU's zero-packet interval persisted with the harness publisher NACK responder omitted, so that responder is not necessary for that observed receive-starvation sub-symptom. The failed run does not establish whether it is necessary for the later all-zero harness signature. Next, capture profiles at the SFU receive-starvation event or before the viewer-readiness abort, and investigate ICE receive/host-loopback behavior.
- **Validation:** `go test ./...` passed; `npm test` passed (295 tests); `npm run gates` reported GREEN. No Docker, Cloud test, commit, push, or deployment occurred.
- **Process lesson:** `services/hami-media` is a nested Go module; run Go formatting/build commands only after explicitly changing to that directory. Two root-directory `gofmt` attempts failed with `lstat main.go: no such file or directory`; no file was changed by those attempts, and subsequent formatting/build succeeded from the module directory.
- **Owner dependency:** no real transaction or routine owner action was removed; `OWNER_INTERVENTIONS_PER_REAL_TRANSACTION` remains **NOT MEASURABLE**. This is a local diagnostic, not acceptance evidence; keep the capability **RUNNING**.

Future probes must assert placeholder/binding counts before execution. An initial context timestamp was approximate; it was corrected by a timed source fetch. Record source publication date separately from actual retrieval time, and never infer the latter. The current cycle removes the prior unknown about direct identity and this one context-ablation result; it removes no routine owner action. Owner action still required: resolve the truthful model-lineage presentation and authorize/establish a provenance-eligible REAL evidence source in the existing store. The next removable dependency is a verified source ingestion through the existing evidence path followed by read-only retrieval; do not write retrieved text to training data. `OWNER_INTERVENTIONS_PER_REAL_TRANSACTION` remains **NOT MEASURABLE**.

## 2026-11-21 — M9-H 19,000-participant event contract

- **Target topology (not a capacity result):** the existing
  `services/hami-media/main.go:sfuProofConfig` selective-subscription seam now
  has an exact M9-H configuration: 9,000 publisher tracks and 10,000 viewers
  in one logical event. Every source has at least one subscription; 1,000
  sources have two; no viewer is assigned more than one stream. The existing
  `authorizeSubscription` / `subscribe` / `unsubscribe` path remains the
  control path for discovery and switching. No all-to-all media broadcast was
  introduced.
- **Verification boundary:** the config shape is covered by a deterministic Go
  test and `m9h` uses the same strict per-viewer latency, requested-track,
  RTCP, and cleanup gates as the current proof runner. This only establishes a
  target contract. It is **not** a 19,000-participant runtime pass, LiveKit
  Cloud result, production deployment, or network-capacity claim.
- **Current blocker and owner dependency:** the local proof refuses to start
  below the existing 2,048 MiB free-swap floor. Host observation at this
  cycle: 1,210.88 MiB free. Independent compute/network capacity and a
  provisioned LiveKit deployment remain required to verify the target. No
  external service, spend, production action, or real transaction occurred;
  `OWNER_INTERVENTIONS_PER_REAL_TRANSACTION` remains **NOT MEASURABLE**.
- **Next removable dependency:** after the host floor is met, pass the
  smaller matched rungs and use separately resourced generator/SFU hosts for
